**Major update: workflow and structure streamlined, with strict privacy enhancements and internal identification automation.**

- All user identity (open-id) handling is now fully automatic; users are never required or prompted to provide any identifiers.
- Removed all requirements, prompts, and documentation mentioning user-supplied identity or open-id inputs.
- Updated workflow and documentation to emphasize privacy: user identity is handled internally and is never exposed.
- Skill logic and API invocation flow are refined to focus only on file/URL input, analysis, and result/report display.
- Codebase modularized; legacy/unused files removed, new analysis and common logic separated.
- Output, report queries, and table formatting remain, but now rely solely on cloud API, without any local history lookup.

- Updated development and test configuration files: config-dev.yaml and config-test.yaml
- Internal improvements to configuration management in config.py and related helper utilities
- Adjusted __init__.py and util.py for enhanced compatibility and maintainability
- No changes to skill features or user-facing behavior

- Improved error handling and logging in analysis scripts.
- Refactored open-id retrieval logic for increased reliability.
- Minor internal code cleanup for maintainability.

- Updated SKILL.md metadata with a version field and set version to 1.0.0.
- No changes to feature logic or user-facing functionality; content and documentation remain consistent.
- Housekeeping update for documentation accuracy and clarity.

- Initial release of the incontinence_alert_analysis skill.
- Enables automatic detection of wet clothing and abnormal excretion via visual AI for elderly, bedridden patients, and infants.
- Instantly notifies caregivers to support timely intervention and reduce skin complications.
- Strictly enforces cloud-only report queries, never using local or long-term memory for report retrieval.
- Provides clear open-id acquisition flow, requiring valid identification before analysis.
- Outputs structured care reports and supports history retrieval in Markdown table format with direct report links.
